Choose $\bmf{\Phi} = \tilde{\bmf{m}}_h^l$, and
  the FVEM scheme \eqref{auxiliary} is equivalent to the FVEM scheme \eqref{equ:LL-semi-discretized1},
  i.e.
  \begin{equation*}
  \lim_{l\rightarrow \infty}\|\bmf{m}_h-\tilde{\bmf{m}}_h^l\|_{\bmf{L}^2} = 0,\quad

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem-con only states that consecutive differences of the iterates go to zero in H^2. It does not establish that the iterates converge to the exact solution in L^2 or H^1, nor that the limit solves the LL equation. The proof also asserts, without proof, that the linearized FVEM scheme with Φ = \tilde m_h^l converges to the nonlinear FVEM scheme. Moreover, Proposition pro2 gives an error bound for each auxiliary problem, but the constant may depend on l; uniform bounds are not provided. Hence the triangle inequality does not prove the stated error estimates.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove convergence of the continuous and discrete linearization iterations to the exact and discrete nonlinear solutions, with uniform constants, and then justify taking the limit.
issues.overall_effect: The main spatial error estimates (error-L2, error-H1) in Theorem thm-error are not established.
issues.title: Error estimate proof assumes unproven convergence of linearization
issues.why_classification: The defect invalidates the proof of the paper's main convergence theorem; repairing it requires a new convergence analysis for the fixed-point iteration and uniform error bounds, i.e., substantial new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The identity m_h·∂t m_h=0 implies that (m_h×∂t m_h)·∂t m_h=0 and that the projections of the potential terms onto ∂t m_h vanish. However, the inner products in the scheme are against I_h^*∂t m_h, not ∂t m_h. Since I_h^* is not the identity, terms such as (m_h×∂t m_h, I_h^*∂t m_h), (ε|∇m_h|² m_h, I_h^*∂t m_h), and ((m_h·hat f)m_h, I_h^*∂t m_h) do not vanish in general. The displayed inequality is therefore not justified.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must correctly handle or bound the dual-test quadrature terms instead of dropping them by an invalid orthogonality argument.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the discrete energy dissipation law (Proposition energy-dissipation) is invalid.
issues.title: Energy dissipation proof drops nonzero dual-test terms
issues.why_classification: The discrete energy dissipation law is a main theoretical claim; the proof's key step is invalid and repairing it requires a new control of the FVEM quadrature terms, not a routine local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: Differentiating the displayed discrete energy gives (ε/2) d_t |||m_h|||_h² - (hat f, I_h^*∂t m_h), not ε d_t |||m_h|||_h². The proof uses the latter to conclude d_t F ≤ 0 from an inequality whose gradient term has coefficient ε(1+α²). The missing factor 1/2 breaks the algebra.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the differentiation to include the factor 1/2 and redo the energy inequality; this may require adjusting the weak form or the energy norm definition.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of the discrete energy dissipation law is numerically inconsistent.
issues.title: Factor 2 error in discrete energy derivative
issues.why_classification: It is a clear algebraic error in a central proof step, but the repair is local once the correct factor is used, although it may affect the final inequality.

issues.failure_explanation: The equations defining g_1 and g_2 use m_i^{n+1}, but m^{n+1} is computed only after the Gauss-Seidel update and projection. Thus the algorithm is circular and not well-defined as written. It likely should use the already computed \hat m_i^{n+1} (or m_i^n), but the source does not specify.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace m_i^{n+1} in the g_i equations by the appropriate already computed iterate, most plausibly \hat m_i^{n+1}.
issues.overall_effect: The GSPM time-marching procedure cannot be executed exactly as stated.
issues.title: GSPM algorithm uses m^{n+1} before it is defined
issues.why_classification: The defect is a single local notational error that, once corrected, preserves the intended algorithm and its stated computational cost.

issues.failure_explanation: The space X does not imply that ∇Φ is in L∞ or that ΔΦ is in L4 pointwise. The proof uses bounds such as ||∇Φ||_{L∞} and ||ΔΦ||_{L4} without assuming them. Hence the constant C need not be finite under the stated hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to require the needed L∞-type bounds on Φ (e.g., Φ∈L∞ W^{1,∞} and suitable L∞ L4 bounds for ΔΦ).
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem-m-H2 and the auxiliary error analysis that relies on it are not justified for arbitrary Φ∈X.
issues.title: Auxiliary lemma assumes insufficient regularity on Φ
issues.why_classification: A standard additional regularity condition fixes the lemma without changing the main method or conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The regularity condition is stated for the solution m of the LL equation, but Proposition pro2 concerns the solution \tilde m of the auxiliary problem with a given Φ. The proof uses bounds on \tilde m and ∂t \tilde m that are not supplied by this condition unless Φ=\tilde m. Thus the hypothesis does not support the proposition as written.
